rejected.title: Finding and organising information
card: Information for an economics or business inquiry can come from many places. Four common ones are government statistics, news reports, businesses and surveys.
Each source is made by someone for a reason. Note who made it, so you can judge whether they might leave out or stress some facts.
Also note when it was made. Prices, jobs and business conditions change, so an old source may no longer be accurate.
Sort what you find under headings, such as the parts of your inquiry question. This makes it easier to compare sources and spot gaps.
rejected.remember: Record who made a source and when, then sort the facts under headings.

a.q: Why should a student note who made a source?
opts: To judge whether the maker might stress some facts
To check that the source uses recent figures
To sort the facts under the right headings
To make sure the source is a government one
a.why: Every source is made by someone for a reason, and that can shape which facts it includes. Noting when it was made is a different step, which checks whether the information is still up to date.
a.clue: Think about the reason the source was made.

b.q: Priya is researching how much teenagers in Hobart spend on snacks. She finds a snack company's website from six years ago. Why should she take care with its figures?
opts: A seller made it, and spending may have changed since
It came from a business, not from government statistics
It is about snacks, not other things teenagers buy
She has not yet sorted it under her inquiry headings
b.why: The maker is a snack company, which may stress facts that help it sell snacks, and the source is six years old, so spending may have changed. Businesses are one of the common sources, so coming from a business rather than the government is not the problem. What matters is who made it and when.
b.clue: Ask who made the source and when.

It shows whether the facts are still current
It tells you which heading to sort it under
It proves that the facts in the source are true

b.q: Priya is looking into what teenagers in Hobart spend on snacks. One source is a survey a snack company ran last month. What should she keep in mind about it?

Sorting it under headings will make it more accurate
